rv.q: Gary pulls off his Fooling. White's midwife, Carol, who appears halfway through Gary's machinations, still alive among the mound of bodies, finds and saves the baby that she believes she'd left to die back in the original play.

Directed with old-fashioned panache by George C. Wolfe, “Gary” proves to be an intermittently amusing but primarily bewildering experience — like a five-minute vaudeville sketch that has been uncomfortably stretched to 95 minutes.

...while the philosophical issues of leadership, class and art don't always land as completely as the expertly-performed wordplay and slapstick, not to mention a rousing spectacle near the finish that is best left as a surprise, Gary: A Sequel to Titus Andronicus is bound inspire further thought about those who create madness in art to inspire r...
